cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Social login lets users sign in with an existing identity provider account such as Google instead of a new password. Sign in with Google uses OpenID Connect: the app receives a Google-signed ID token, and Google handles passwords and MFA.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Work splits across Google Cloud Console (create OAuth client IDs), the Android app (Credential Manager), the backend (verify the token, issue own tokens) and the database (fields like social_id, social_provider, is_email_verified). The backend verifies signature, issuer, expiry and that aud equals its client ID, then finds or creates the user.

questions.q: Can the backend trust the email the app sends with the token?
questions.a: No. It must trust only claims inside an ID token it has verified itself: Google signature, iss, exp and aud.

questions.q: What does the backend issue after verifying the Google token?
questions.a: Its own access and refresh tokens for the rest of the session.

questions.q: Which protocol powers Sign in with Google?
questions.a: OpenID Connect, the identity layer built on OAuth 2.0.
